cf.title: Release replication slot on error in SQL-callable slot functions

input.subject: [PATCH] Release replication slot on error in SQL-callable slot functions

verdict_reasoning: The bug is reproducible with plain SQL and the goal is not in dispute. One fixable level 2 objection survived, standards-compat-1: releasing the slot on subtransaction abort changes what extensions see in minor releases back to PG14, and the thread reviewed only the commit side. That is a back-patch risk judgement for a committer who knows the slot code. It does not stop the idea.

brief.title: Release replication slot when a subtransaction that acquired it aborts
brief.problem: SQL slot functions set MyReplicationSlot and can error before releasing the slot. If a PL/pgSQL (or PL/Perl, PL/Python, PL/Tcl) exception block catches the error, the top-level cleanup never runs. The next slot call hits an assertion, or in release builds the slot stays active, holding back WAL removal and vacuum.
brief.proposed_design: The first versions wrapped each slot function in PG_TRY/PG_CATCH. From v7 on, the patch records the subtransaction id that acquired the slot and releases the slot in a new subtransaction-end callback when that subtransaction aborts. Temporary slots are not dropped on a caught error, and nothing happens on subtransaction commit.
user_visible_surface: Documentation change: temporary slots are dropped on errors, but not on an error caught in a subtransaction such as a PL/pgSQL exception block.
A slot acquired in a subtransaction is now released when that subtransaction aborts, which changes behavior for extensions that hold slots.
author_claims: The bug exists on all supported branches back to PG14 and is reachable with plain SQL.
Affected functions include slot create, copy, advance, drop, and the get/peek changes functions.
pg_sync_replication_slots() is not affected because it already uses PG_ENSURE_ERROR_CLEANUP().
Releasing the slot during subtransaction abort cannot raise an error (Sawada's reading of the code).
The fix is meant for back-patching to all supported branches.
brief.thread_state: Many reviewers (Sawada, Shveta, Amit, Hou, Ashutosh, Horiguchi) shaped v19, and Sawada said in message #86 he planned to push. Leftover temporary slots after a failed create were moved to a separate thread.
unclear: The thread does not say whether v19 was committed or which branches got it.
Horiguchi's suggestion to use ResourceOwner instead of a subtransaction-end callback got no visible reply.
The material shows commit messages for v1 and v5 only, not for the v19 design.
The thread does not say how a slot held across transactions by an extension behaves after this change.

objections.title: Release on subtransaction abort changes extension-visible slot state in minor releases
objections.failure_scenario: An extension acquires a slot inside BeginInternalSubTransaction(), catches an error with PG_CATCH, calls RollbackAndReleaseCurrentSubTransaction() and then calls ReplicationSlotRelease(). After the minor update the rollback has already cleared MyReplicationSlot, so the extension's release call fails an assertion or dereferences a NULL slot. The user finds out when the backend crashes on the first decoding error after the update.
objections.argument: The thread studied the commit side for extensions in detail and removed the handoff and WARNING to avoid minor-release changes (messages #70, #73, #81). The abort side gets no such review, but it is the part that now runs inside AbortSubTransaction() on every supported branch back to PG14. Existing extension cleanup code was written for a world where slot state survives a subtransaction rollback. The v19 commit message is not in the material, so it is unknown whether release notes will warn extension authors.
objections.author_must_show: Was extension code that releases the slot after rolling back its own subtransaction checked, and will the back-branch commit message or release notes tell extension authors about the new abort behavior?

critic.reasoning: The thread reviewed the commit path for extensions (#70, #73) but not an extension that calls ReplicationSlotRelease() after rolling back its own subtransaction. Amit's remark in #58 accepts the new restriction without covering this crash on back branches.

refuted.title: Back-branch release on subxact abort changes behavior for extensions
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension acquires a slot inside BeginInternalSubTransaction(), catches an error with RollbackAndReleaseCurrentSubTransaction(), and keeps using MyReplicationSlot. After a minor upgrade the abort callback has released the slot, so the next access finds MyReplicationSlot NULL and the backend crashes, or another session takes the slot. The user finds out in production, after the minor release.
refuted.argument: Message #73 rejected a commit-path change in back branches because it would change, in a minor release, a pattern that "works today on all branches". The abort path changes in the same way, and message #33 noted that it also fires on a manual abort with no error. No message checks this abort case against code that intentionally keeps the slot after rolling back its own subtransaction. Messages #78 and #79 treat such cases as hypothetical, which is a judgement, and the material contains no survey of extensions.
refuted.author_must_show: Does any known extension or decoding framework acquire a slot in a subtransaction it may roll back and then keep using it, and how was this checked?

critic.reasoning: Duplicate of standards-compat-1, which gives the more concrete scenario for the same back-branch abort behavior change.

refuted.title: Subxact-end callback chosen over ResourceOwner without a stated reason
refuted.failure_scenario: An extension acquires a slot inside an inner subtransaction, which commits, and the enclosing subtransaction then aborts on a caught error. v19 clears MyReplicationSlotSubId on the inner commit, so the outer abort does not release the slot. The next slot call in that session hits the assertion, or in release builds leaves the slot active.
refuted.argument: Message #55 suggests ResourceOwner because ownership passing to the parent on commit is what it already does, and the thread shows no reply. Messages #73 and #80 dropped the handoff to avoid a behavior change in minor releases. That leaves a new private mechanism with weaker coverage than the existing one. A committer would likely ask why the new design departs from ResourceOwner, the usual way core ties a resource to a (sub)transaction.
refuted.author_must_show: Why is a dedicated AtEOSubXact callback better than registering the acquired slot with the current ResourceOwner, at least on HEAD?

critic.reasoning: The scenario is today's behavior, and messages #73 and #80 left it unchanged on purpose to keep the back-branch fix small. A subtransaction-end callback copies existing practice such as AtEOSubXact_LargeObject() and AtEOSubXact_Files(), so item 12 does not fail.

touch_points.label: WAL / replication / standby
touch_points.reason: The patch changes when a backend releases a replication slot, which affects WAL retention by an active slot.

touch_points.label: ABI / extension API
touch_points.reason: A slot that an extension acquires in a subtransaction is now released when that subtransaction aborts.

touch_points.label: backpatchability
touch_points.reason: The fix is meant for all supported branches back to PG14 and changes slot behavior on subtransaction abort there.

touch_points.label: maintenance burden ("who maintains this in 10 years")
touch_points.reason: The patch adds a subtransaction-end callback and a recorded subtransaction id that slot code must keep correct.

touch_points.label: performance on the hot path
touch_points.reason: The new callback runs at every subtransaction end, and the review notes put the cost at one variable comparison.

touch_points.label: doesn't fit what Postgres is about (extension / external tool / already solved)

questions: Was extension code that calls ReplicationSlotRelease() after rolling back its own subtransaction checked against the new abort behavior?
Will the back-branch commit message or release notes tell extension authors that a subtransaction abort now releases the slot?
Should the abort-time release go to all branches back to PG14, or should back branches get a narrower fix?
How does a slot that an extension holds across transactions behave after this change?
Why is a subtransaction-end callback preferred over ResourceOwner, as message #55 suggested, at least on HEAD?

committability.owner_note: Sawada reviewed the design and said in message #86 that he planned to push. The owner needs to know the replication slot code and subtransaction abort processing.
committability.liability: The owner signs for slot release inside AbortSubTransaction() on every supported branch back to PG14, including any extension breakage that shows up after a minor release.
committability.author_follow_up: The patch went through 19 versions over about 90 messages with many reviewers, which suggests the authors stay engaged.

priority.reason: Only sessions that catch a slot function error in a subtransaction hit the bug, but the result is an assertion failure or a slot stuck active that holds back WAL removal and vacuum. The v19 patch was not read; early versions are small and touch slot code only.

provisional_note: The material shows commit messages for v1 and v5 only, so the v19 callback design and its claim that release cannot raise an error during subtransaction abort were not checked. The thread does not say whether v19 was committed.
disclosure: Prepared by an AI harness; treat as a devil's advocate, not a verdict.

precedents_retrieved.title: Error "initial slot snapshot too large" in create replication slot
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch fixes the "initial slot snapshot too large" error in CREATE_REPLICATION_SLOT, which happens because SnapBuildInitialSnapshot puts top-level and subtransaction XIDs into the xip array and the count can exceed GetMaxSnapshotXidCount(). Versions tried excluding subtransactions, marking the snapshot takenDuringRecovery, asking the reorder buffer which XIDs are subtransactions, and finally using the subxip array as an extension of xip.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Robert Haas objected to the last version because it adds a third way of using the xip and subxip arrays, and he saw no consensus on an approach. Earlier approaches failed for other reasons: the reorder buffer cannot reliably tell subtransactions apart, using takenDuringRecovery was rejected, and resizing xip made procarray.c and snapmgr.c too complicated. The author withdrew the entry for lack of a simple fix.
matched_queries: temporary replication slot not dropped error
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
It's bad enough that we
already use the xip/subxip arrays in two different ways depending on
the situation. Increasing that to three different ways seems painful.

precedents_retrieved.title: Reuse Workers and Replication Slots during Logical Replication
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch lets a tablesync worker, after it finishes one table, pick up the next table in init state and sync it, keeping its replication slot. This removes the cost of starting a new worker and creating and dropping a slot for each table, which matters most for many empty or small tables.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Benchmarks by reviewers showed regressions in some settings, and the v28 design #2 results were up to about twice as slow as HEAD and varied widely between runs. The patch also no longer applied to HEAD. Amit Kapila proposed Returned with feedback because the regressions still needed analysis, and vignesh C asked for a new entry with a fix for the regression.
matched_queries: temporary replication slot not dropped error
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
IIRC, there were some regressions observed with this patch. So, one
needs to analyze those as well.

precedents_retrieved.title: Add function pg_advance_replication_slot
precedents_retrieved.summary: Add a SQL function that moves a physical replication slot forward to a given WAL position without consuming the WAL, for example to keep slots in sync across servers. Later versions named it pg_advance_replication_slot, allowed forward moves only, and raised an error on logical slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Michael Paquier asked that moving the slot backwards raise an error with the current slot position instead of a warning, and that the logical-slot error use ERRCODE_FEATURE_NOT_SUPPORTED. Andres Freund added that neither message followed the message style guidelines. The patch got no update in the following two months, so it was returned with feedback.
matched_queries: temporary replication slot not dropped error
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
True as well, and the patch did not get an update in two months to
reflect that. So I am marking it as returned with feedback.

precedents_retrieved.title: Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Track invalidation_reason in pg_replication_slots.
Reverted commit(s): Track conflict_reason in pg_replication_slots.
precedents_retrieved.objection:
Till now, the reason for replication slot invalidation is not tracked
directly in pg_replication_slots. A recent commit 007693f2a3 added
'conflict_reason' to show the reasons for slot conflict/invalidation, but
only for logical slots.

This commit adds a new column 'invalidation_reason' to show invalidation
reasons for both physical and logical slots. And, this commit also turns
'conflict_reason' text column to 'conflicting' boolean column (effectively
reverting commit 007693f2a3). The 'conflicting' column is true for
invalidation reasons 'rows_removed' and 'wal_level_insufficient' because
those make the slot conflict with recovery. When 'conflicting' is true,
one can now look at the new 'invalidation_reason' column for the reason
for the logical slot's conflict with recovery.

The new 'invalidation_reason' column will also be useful to track other
invalidation reasons in the future commit.

precedents_retrieved.title: pg_replslotdata - a tool for displaying replication slot information
precedents_retrieved.objectors: Andres Freund, Michael Paquier, Julien Rouhaud
precedents_retrieved.summary: A new client-side tool, pg_replslotdata, reads the binary replication slot files under pg_replslot/ and prints slot information such as restart LSN, xid, slot type and two-phase state. It works while the server is down, in the same way as pg_controldata and pg_waldump.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Committers judged that the use cases did not justify the cost of maintaining a separate tool in core, including its documentation and translations, and that most needs can be met with an online server. Since the tool is entirely client side, reviewers suggested keeping it in an external repository. The author agreed to drop the patch.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
Weighed against the cost of maintaining (including documentation) a separate
tool this doesn't seem sufficient reason.

precedents_retrieved.title: Forbid the use of invalidated physical slots in streaming replication.
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch makes StartReplication() reject a physical replication slot that has already been invalidated, for example by max_slot_wal_keep_size, as the logical walsender already does. Without it a walsender can stream from an invalidated slot, move its restart_lsn forward, and pg_replication_slots shows it as valid while it protects neither WAL nor rows.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author stopped responding to review questions, so vignesh C moved the entry to Waiting on Author and then to Returned with Feedback. Ashutosh Bapat asked how a build before commit 15f8203 behaves and warned that changing long-released behaviour of physical slots could break backward compatibility. Robert Haas noted that the documentation does not match the current behaviour and that the intended interaction with physical slots is not clear.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
I think making logical and physical slot behaviour consistent would be
better but if the inconsistent behaviour is out there for some
releases, changing that now will break backward compatibility.

precedents_retrieved.title: Skip replicating the tables specified in except table option
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch adds an EXCEPT TABLE clause to CREATE/ALTER PUBLICATION ... FOR ALL TABLES, which records excluded tables in pg_publication_rel and makes pgoutput skip their changes. A companion patch adds ALTER PUBLICATION ... RESET, which returns a publication to its default state before ALL TABLES with an exception list is added.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The author withdrew the patch after the thread went quiet. From mid-2022 the messages are rebases and commitfest reminders, and the author said he saw little interest from others. Earlier, Peter Eisentraut doubted the feature was worth the trouble and pointed to the cost of tracking negative dependencies. Peter Smith found the meaning of ALTER PUBLICATION combined with EXCEPT ambiguous, but these points did not decide the outcome.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote:
As I did not see much interest from others, I'm withdrawing this patch
for now.

precedents_retrieved.title: Synchronize logical replication slots from primary to standby
precedents_retrieved.summary: A background worker on a physical standby periodically fetches logical replication slot information from the primary, so that after failover a logical subscriber finds up-to-date slots on the new primary. Later versions added synchronize_slot_names on the standby to pick which slots to sync, and standby_slot_names on the primary to hold logical replication back until the listed physical standbys catch up.
precedents_retrieved.objection: Andres Freund found that the patch breaks the catalog_xmin guarantee: row versions still needed for logical decoding on the standby can be removed. He said it needs a mechanism such as the "Minimal logical decoding on standbys" patch, which the author said was not near ready. Reviewers also objected to the blocking wait and the per-commit work added to reorderbuffer.c, and to the worker-per-database design tied to the logical replication launcher. The author listed these and an open configuration design as significant jobs still to do.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The patch as-is just breaks one of the fundamental guarantees necessary for logical decoding, that no rows versions can be removed that are still required for logical decoding (signalled via catalog_xmin).

precedents_retrieved.title: Cleanup gcc trick with varattrib_1b_e in VARATT_EXTERNAL_GET_POINTER()
precedents_retrieved.summary: The patch removes the intermediate "varattrib_1b_e *" variable from VARATT_EXTERNAL_GET_POINTER() in detoast.h, which was added years ago to work around gcc producing code that assumed aligned datum contents. The goal was to stop code from referencing varattrib_1b_e directly.
precedents_retrieved.objection: The entry was withdrawn, and no message gives the author's own reason. Nathan Bossart said the patch saves only a few lines of code, while removing the workaround needs confidence that the gcc problem is gone. Tom Lane argued the problem may still exist because compilers now optimize more aggressively on dubious assumptions, and misaligned accesses are still expensive on many platforms.
precedents_retrieved.key_quote: The risk/reward ratio might not be favorable on this one.

precedents_retrieved.title: Don't allow to EXECUTE empty queries (fixes Assert violation)
precedents_retrieved.authors: Tom Lane (tgl), Aleksander Alekseev (a.alekseev), Alexander Lakhin (law)
precedents_retrieved.summary:
Don't allow to EXECUTE empty queries (fixes Assert violation)
Threads: BUG #18984: Empty prepared statement from psql \parse triggers assert in PortalRunMulti

roaster_notes.note: No precedent found: the precedent search returned no earlier attempt at this idea. The thread mentions no earlier discussion of it either, and the only related thread it names is a split-off for temporary slots whose creation fails (message #90).
The SQL-level contract does not change. No syntax, GUC, catalog or pg_dump change is involved, and the documentation hunk describes what already happens to temporary slots.

The patch adds no on-disk, WAL, catalog or protocol change. The release runs only in-process memory and existing slot code during subxact abort, and message #56 argues it cannot raise an error there. Leftover temporary slots after a failed create are a pre-existing issue and were moved to a separate thread.

The fix adds no new privilege, function, or exposure; the slot functions keep requiring superuser or the REPLICATION attribute. Releasing the slot on subtransaction abort removes a session-local leak that held back WAL removal and vacuum. Temporary slots left behind after a failed create already behaved this way and were moved to a separate thread.

Apart from the ResourceOwner question, maintenance and fit look sound. The fix is a backpatchable bug fix in core code, several committers in this area reviewed it, and the per-subxact cost is one variable comparison.

This is a crash and resource-leak fix with no existing alternative. Users cannot avoid it short of not catching errors, and PG_ENSURE_ERROR_CLEANUP (used by pg_sync_replication_slots()) would need per-function wrapping, which the thread weighed and dropped. Horiguchi's ResourceOwner suggestion in message #55 got no reply, but an AtEOSubXact callback follows the existing practice of AtEOSubXact_LargeObject() and AtEOSubXact_Files(), so I see no concrete failure scenario to raise from this angle.

This is a bug fix, so the demand bar is low. Plain SQL in a PL/pgSQL exception block can crash an assert build, and in a release build it leaves a slot active that holds back WAL removal and vacuum. Several reviewers reproduced it independently (messages #1, #3, #5, #7, #74), and there is no workaround short of ending the session. The cost falls on the subtransaction abort path only when a slot is held.
